narrative:
The model estimates a 45% chance that you will leave your job. This is high enough for the company to deny your promotion, as they prefer to invest in people more likely to stay long-term.

The decision was driven mainly by three factors, ranked by importance. First, your total years of experience across all jobs had the strongest influence, pushing the prediction toward you staying. At 1-5 years, you fall into the most common group among employees the model expects to remain, which the system sees as a stabilizing factor. Second, not having received other job offers while at the company also pulled the prediction toward staying, since most people predicted to stay (77%) similarly report no external opportunities.

However, the third most important factor worked against you. Your low level of involvement in decision-making and difficulty getting your opinions heard pushed the prediction noticeably toward leaving. This sense of limited voice appears to outweigh the stabilizing effects of your experience and lack of outside offers in the model's eyes.

The organization should consider discussing ways to increase your participation in decisions and gather your input more effectively. For you, reflecting on whether greater engagement would improve your commitment could help clarify your future plans. Addressing this area might change both your experience and future promotion prospects. (218 words)
